name: Sea kale

schedule.notes: Plant root cuttings (thongs) 2 in deep. Faster than seed. Pick a permanent spot — lives 10+ years.
Year 3+: cover with a clay pot in early spring; harvest blanched white shoots 6 to 8 weeks later. Don't harvest in year 1 or 2.

harvest.cues: Shoots 6 to 10 in tall under the cover, white and tender. Cut at the base; uncover to let plant photosynthesize.
harvest.storageNotes: Best fresh — turns green and bitter on exposure to light within hours. Wrapped tightly in foil, fridge 2 days.

varieties.name: Common Sea Kale
varieties.notes: The traditional Victorian-garden vegetable. Blanched stems taste like a cross between asparagus and hazelnut.

notes: Victorian luxury crop, nearly extinct from gardens. Cover crowns in late winter with terracotta pots, straw, or buckets — exclude light. Harvested young shoots are an exquisite delicacy. Plants get massive (3 to 4 ft) with cabbage-like flowers and seedpods.
